note: What the manufacturer's own documentation says about the console's memory timing, and what this project derives from it. Every figure here is either quoted from the document named below or shown as arithmetic on figures that are. This file is the authority on the numbers the layout module counts in. When an implementation disagrees with it, the implementation is wrong.

order: hardware.json, for anything Nintendo printed and anything that follows from it by arithmetic shown here
the corpus, for header combinations read out of real cartridges
neither overrides the other, because they answer different questions
authority.why: The access-cycle counts every emulator uses are correct, but an emulator is not why they are correct. All three follow from the speeds the manual prints, two in the Map Mode table and the third in section 21.1, and Figure 2-21-1 says which addresses run at which.

comparedAgainst.what: The headers of every retail cartridge in a real library, which is the artifact rather than a description of it.

busSpeeds.note: These are the two speeds a cartridge selects between in its header, row 20H and row 30H of the table. Both of this project's cartridge access counts follow from them.

cpuClockSpeeds.quote: Three clock speeds are available: 3.58MHz, 2.68MHz, and 1.79 MHz.
cpuClockSpeeds.note: The text layer prints the third as 1 .79 MHz. The page image of printed page 2-21-1 reads 1.79 MHz, and the flattened text the checker compares is the same either way.

controllerRegion.section: Figure 2-21-1, Super NES CPU Memory Map, printed page 2-21-2
controllerRegion.readFrom: The page image only, because the text layer carries the caption and none of the figure. Rendered at 110 and again at 250 dots per inch, cropped to the address legend; both readings agree.

masterClockHz.derivation: Six times the NTSC colour carrier, 3579545.4545 Hz, rounded to the nearest hertz. The console counts in this.
masterClockHz.note: Not from Book I. It is the standard NTSC relationship, and it is what makes the arithmetic below come out whole.

fastAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477272 / 3.58 MHz = 5.9992, so six master cycles, and six master cycles back the other way is 3.5795 MHz, which is the 3.58 MHz the manual prints.
fastAccessMasterCycles.note: Derived from a documented figure rather than taken from an implementation. The rounding is in the manual's own printing of the speed, not in this.

slowAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477272 / 2.68 MHz = 8.0139, so eight master cycles, and eight master cycles back the other way is 2.6847 MHz, which the manual prints as 2.68 MHz.

extraSlowAccessMasterCycles.derivation: 21477273 / 1.79 MHz = 11.998, so twelve master cycles, and twelve master cycles back the other way is 1.7898 MHz, which the manual prints as 1.79 MHz.
extraSlowAccessMasterCycles.note: Derived from the third speed section 21.1 prints, for the region Figure 2-21-1 labels CONTROLLER.

notCycleAccurate.note: What this project does and does not claim, so a reader does not inherit a stronger belief than the evidence supports.
notCycleAccurate.does: Reports how many master cycles an access to a resolved address costs, from the three speeds the manual prints.
doesNot: Model the CPU. How many accesses an instruction makes, and therefore what it costs, belongs to the processor rather than to the map.
Model refresh, DMA stalls, or the cycles the console spends on anything other than the access itself.

developmentManual.title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System Development Manual, Book I
developmentManual.note: Searched for a table of access cycles per region and for cycle counts in master clocks. It has neither. It prints three CPU clock speeds in section 21.1 and in Figure 2-21-1, and the two a cartridge selects in the Map Mode table, and that is enough for all three figures this project uses.
developmentManual.section: Map Mode table, page 1-2-17, and section 21.1, page 2-21-1
developmentManual.whatThatDigestIs: The copy this address served on 2026-08-27, fetched and held on the machine that records it. It identifies what was read rather than confirming it against an older pin, because no pin existed before: the figures had been read from a transcription at an archive with nothing on disk to hash. The two speeds and the Map Mode table were confirmed in the fetched copy, on the run of text that ends at printed page 1-2-17, which is where the record already said they sit.
